name: Matthan
overview: Matthan was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Eleazar within the lineage of the Messiah. His identity is grounded in his place in the genealogical record that traces the ancestry of Jesus Christ, highlighting his role in the providential history of redemption.
namesAndTitles: The name Matthan is a proper name meaning "gift," though it was not given by God. This meaning underscores the biblical theme of divine blessing and provision, fitting for one in the Messiah’s ancestral line.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Matthan was the father of Jacob and, inferred from the genealogy, the son of Eleazar. These relationships situate him directly within the Messianic lineage as outlined in Matthew 1:15.
scriptureSignificance: Matthan’s significance lies in his position within the genealogy of Jesus Christ, as documented in Matthew 1:15. By linking Eleazar to Jacob, he forms a crucial link in the ancestral chain through which the Messiah was born, affirming the fulfillment of God’s promises to the tribe of Judah and the house of David.
